## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At death_q=0.01, ns/p drops from 11.9 at N=4000 to 7.931 at N=16000 — overhead amortization at small N. From N=16000 through N=4000000 the cost stays FLAT (7.738–8.048 ns/p), with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill (N≈58254). The L1d spill (N≈910) falls below the smallest measured N, so its effect is already absorbed into the N=4000 overhead. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: at q=0.05 the flat region sits at 8.54–9.362 ns/p, and at q=0.25 at 11.83–11.947 ns/p — uniformly higher but still kneeless across N. The absence of any cost rise at the L2 spill confirms the algo is not streaming-bandwidth-limited at any N.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.3 GB/s at N=65000, death_q=0.01 — 37% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound: the flat ns/p across all N (no DRAM-streaming knee) and sub-40% ceiling utilization both indicate cost is dominated by per-particle arithmetic and control flow, not memory transfer. Death rate drives a monotonic bandwidth collapse: 9.3 GB/s at q=0.01 → 8.43 GB/s at q=0.05 → 6.04 GB/s at q=0.25, all flat across N. The transition is purely by death rate, not by N — the branchy respawn path (`bl _Random.init__anon_32866.gen.fill`, the `clz`/`eor`/`ror` PRNG chain) rises with churn and erodes throughput. PMC cycle attribution is unavailable.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of one particle, not across particles. The position/velocity update loads a 128-bit block (`ldur q16, [x9, #-0x10]`), performs a 4-wide multiply-add (`fmul.4s v7, v18, v3`; `fadd.4s v7, v16, v7`), and stores back (`stur q7`). A 2-wide variant (`fmul.2s`, `fadd.2s`) handles the next two floats. There is a gather: `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x10]` inserts a scalar from a separate offset into a vector lane; `ext.16b` plus `mov.s v18[3]` reshuffles lanes to assemble the operand. The scatter section (from 0x100055a80) is entirely scalar: 19 `strb` byte stores with `ldrb` loads, `csel` clamping to 0xff, and `fcmp`/`fcvtzs` conversions — no vectorization. Component-wise vec on contiguous 72-byte strides explains the moderate 9.3 GB/s; the scalar byte-granular scatter and branchy respawn cap it at 37% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak achieved bandwidth never exceeds 9.3 GB/s (37% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at death_q=0.01, N=65000, and the ns/p curve is flat across all N with no cache-spill knee, confirming the algo is compute/overhead-bound rather than streaming-limited. The component-wise auto-vectorization (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`) does not approach the streaming ceiling because the scalar byte-granular scatter (19 `strb`) and branchy respawn path dominate cost, collapsing throughput to 6.04 GB/s by q=0.25.
